analysis: What changed versus the 6:00 AM brief: the hot CPI print has now been priced through the open, and the tape is doing exactly what the futures signaled — lower, with tech leading down. The Dow (-0.47%) is holding up better than the Nasdaq (-0.70%) at 9:48 AM ET, the same rate-sensitivity split seen in futures. The 10-year jumped to 4.988% (+12.6 bps from Monday's 4.862% close) and the 2-year is up 14 bps to 4.697%, with December hike odds above 85% per CME FedWatch — the market has moved from debating whether Waller's 50bp condition was met to pricing a hike as near-certain. Nvidia is the story inside the story: the early +1.3% premarket bounce on the Trump comment has fully reversed into a -4.72% slide to $170.23, extending the five-session loss to -15.75%. The new primary-source color is Huang's letter to staff about the affair (Axios, Nov 8), which Hacker News is dissecting at scale (968 points, 1,248 comments) — the discussion centers on governance and the House timeline, not fundamentals, and the stock is trading the investigation, not the Nov 17 earnings print. The megacap split is telling: Amazon (+1.09%) and Alphabet (+0.23%) are green while Tesla, Microsoft, Apple and Meta are modestly red — a selective give-back of Monday's 1.2-5.5% gains rather than a rout. Oil is the one disinflationary offset still working: WTI ~$84.65, down from Monday's $86.85 settle. Signal vs noise: the CPI beat, the yield jump, and the Nvidia governance slide are the signal; the overnight WSB 'CPI pumps no matter what' mood is noise — the tape is lower, not higher. What matters into the rest of the session is whether the S&P holds 7,500, whether Nvidia stabilizes above $170, and what Fed speakers Logan (10:50 AM ET) and Bowman (3:30 PM ET) say about the hike path after the print.

community_signals.takeaway: The 1,248-comment discussion of Huang's staff letter centers on governance and the House investigation timeline rather than Nvidia's fundamentals — reinforcing that the stock is trading the probe, not the Nov 17 earnings print.

headlines.headline: Stocks opened lower after the hot October CPI print: at 9:48 AM ET the Dow was -0.47% at 52,144.30, the S&P 500 -0.58% at 7,506.25 and the Nasdaq Composite -0.70% at 25,076.22. SPY was down 0.7% and QQQ down 0.9% just after the bell. October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% expected) and core 0.3% (vs +0.2% expected).
headlines.why_it_matters: The open confirmed the futures signal — Monday's +2.35% S&P rally is giving back a slice on the rate repricing, with the Nasdaq hit hardest, exactly the rate-sensitive leg.

headlines.headline: Treasury yields jumped after the CPI print: the 10-year stood at 4.988% at 9:48 AM ET, up from Monday's 4.862% close (+12.6 bps), and the 2-year was up 14 bps at 4.697%. Odds of a December rate hike were greater than 85% per the CME FedWatch Tool, with the door left open for further tightening in January.
headlines.why_it_matters: A 12.6bp jump in the 10-year in one morning is the repricing doing the work — higher yields are the direct headwind for growth and chip names, and the >85% hike odds show the December decision is now treated as near-settled.

headlines.headline: Nvidia extended its slide in early trading: NVDA was -4.72% at $170.23 as of 9:53 AM ET (open $173.97, low $170.12), after a +1.3% premarket bounce on the Trump 'I believe him' comment fully reversed. The five-session loss is now -15.75%. New primary-source color: CEO Jensen Huang's letter to staff about the affair (Axios, Nov 8) is being widely discussed; his reply to the House chairmen is due tomorrow, Nov 11, ahead of a Nov 18 closed-door briefing. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17 (expected EPS $2.53, revenue $111.4B per Finnhub consensus).
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce fading into a fresh -4.7% decline despite analyst support (Mizuho $250 target, Goldman Buy, Bernstein Outperform) shows the stock is still trading the investigation timeline, not fundamentals — and $170 is the next line to watch.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split at the open: Amazon +1.09% ($269.85) and Alphabet +0.23% ($288.80) were green, while Tesla -0.65% ($375.58), Microsoft -0.61% ($541.88), Apple -0.37% ($349.39) and Meta -0.19% ($640.14) were lower as of ~9:53 AM ET. All six gained 1.2-5.5% in Monday's rally. Earnings context: AAPL Q4 FY2026 (Nov 2) EPS $2.10 on $114.5B revenue; MSFT Q1 FY2027 (Oct 28) EPS $4.89 on $92.3B; AMZN Q3 (Oct 29) EPS $1.89 on $201.9B; META Q3 (Oct 21) EPS $7.40 on $64.6B; GOOGL Q3 (Oct 28) EPS $2.67 on $127.6B; TSLA Q3 (Oct 21) EPS $0.48 on $28.0B.
headlines.why_it_matters: A selective give-back, not a rout — two of the seven are holding Monday's gains, which suggests the group is digesting the rate repricing rather than breaking down.

headlines.headline: Anthropic set its IPO terms: the Claude maker will offer 825 million shares at $70-78 per share, an implied valuation above $1 trillion, which would make it one of the biggest publicly traded U.S. companies on arrival.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest private AI name is pricing into public markets right in the middle of the AI-valuation wobble — a test of whether appetite for AI paper survives the rate repricing.

headlines.headline: Early-session movers: Take-Two Interactive surged more than 5% and Marriott climbed nearly 1% among Nasdaq-100 leaders just after the open, while Sandisk tumbled nearly 4% and Rocket Lab fell more than 2% in morning action.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stock-specific moves are still cutting through the macro tape — Take-Two's jump shows buyers are still discriminating rather than selling everything.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning; units -0.82% at $25.27 in early trading, tracking the broader energy pullback as WTI slid to ~$84.65. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.32M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, in line), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. The J-W Power acquisition (~$860M, closed Jan 2026) lifted the fleet to ~4.4M active horsepower. Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September.
